summary.text: Mounts a named Docker volume at the k3s data directory so cluster state persists across AppHost restarts.

remarks.text: , which contains the SQLite database, TLS certificates, and kubeconfig. Without this volume the cluster starts fresh on every AppHost launch. Combine with
on the cluster resource and its dependent Helm releases to avoid re-installing charts on every start.

children.text: The server node also keeps its identity: it registers under the resource name (
), and its node password lives in a second volume at
. Without both, a recreated container — a new k3s version, a changed argument — registers as a new node with a new hostname, and every persistent volume bound to the old node stays pending.

A data volume created before the node name was fixed holds a node named after its old container's hostname, whose password was never kept. Its first start registers a new node under the resource name; persistent volumes bound to the old node must be recreated.

summary.text: Extension methods for serving the AppHost's developer certificate from the k3s cluster.
The name of the TLS Secret that holds the developer certificate, in
kube-system
and in the namespace of every Helm release of the cluster.
Serves the AppHost's developer certificate — the one the machine trusts — from the cluster's bundled Traefik ingress controller, and makes it available to the cluster's workloads.

children.text: The certificate is stored as the TLS Secret

and in the namespace of every Helm release of the cluster, and is made Traefik's default certificate: every host Traefik serves without a certificate of its own is served with it, so a browser on the machine trusts what answers. The developer certificate carries
, so publish hosts under that domain.
In a release's namespace a chart can name the Secret for its ingress and mount its

as a trusted certificate — the certificate is self-signed, so workloads that call each other through the ingress trust it as it is. The Secret holds the private key: this is a local development convenience, and only applies in run mode.

Every Helm release and manifest of the cluster waits for the certificate to be stored. The certificate is stored again on every start, so a renewed developer certificate reaches the cluster without recreating it.

summary.text: Extension methods for the k3s cluster's DNS: making Aspire resources resolvable from pods, and adding CoreDNS configuration.

remarks.text: Pods resolve names through the cluster's CoreDNS, which forwards to the node's resolver. Inside a container that resolver is Docker's embedded DNS on a loopback address, which pods cannot reach — so a pod cannot find another Aspire container by name, nor resolve
. These methods fill the gap through k3s's documented extension point, the
ConfigMap, which a helper container writes once the cluster is ready and before any Helm release or manifest of the cluster runs.
